# Pyret on GitHub

You got here from **Work on GitHub** in code.pyret.org. Your code is on your clipboard.

1. If a box in the bottom-right asks to install the recommended extension, click **Install**.
   (No box? Open the Extensions view, search for "Pyret Interactive Editor", and install it.)
2. When asked "Import your code from code.pyret.org?", click **Import**, then confirm the file name.
3. Your code opens in a Pyret editor. Changes are kept in this browser until you commit.

**To save for real:** open Source Control (the branch icon on the left), type a message, and click
**Commit & Push**. You can't push to this shared repository, so you'll be offered a fork: accept it.
Your fork is your own copy on GitHub, and it is **public**.

Already have code on your clipboard but no prompt? Run **Pyret: Import code from code.pyret.org (clipboard)**
from the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P), or create a new `.arr` file and paste.
